title: Sep 2 Results: When the Favorites Don't Show Up
summary: A tough 6-9 day as heavy favorites stumbled across the board

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Baseball

Sometimes the game just doesn't care about your confidence levels. September 2nd was one of those humbling days where our strongest picks—the ones we felt really good about—decided to teach us a lesson in baseball unpredictability. We finished 6-9, hitting just 40% of our predictions. Ouch.

## The High-Confidence Heartbreaks

The really tough part? Our highest confidence picks were the ones that hurt most. The Blue Jays at 62% delivered, thankfully. But the Mariners pick at 61%? The Orioles at 61%? The Rays at 61%? All three went down. When you're betting on the favorites and they don't show up, that's when a day goes sideways fast.

content.value:
## The Bright Spots

Let's not bury the wins completely. The Blue Jays came through as our top pick, justifying that 62% confidence. The Giants squeaked out a win in Pittsburgh at 56%, and the Braves handled business against the Nationals at 52%. These weren't coin flips—they were solid reads that held up when it mattered.

## What Went Wrong

The story of the day was favorites failing to live up to expectations. The Orioles losing to the Rockies in Colorado? That's baseball in the thin air. The Rays falling to the Mets? New York's been scrappy. The White Sox beating the Mariners? Well, even a struggling team wins sometimes.

But here's what these misses tell us: September baseball is different. Teams are fighting for playoff position or playing spoiler. The urgency changes everything, and sometimes the numbers from August don't translate to September reality.

content.title: 💭 Lesson Learned
content.value: High confidence doesn't guarantee wins—it just means we liked the matchup.
content.sub: Baseball always gets the last word

content.value:
## Looking Ahead

No games tomorrow means we get a rare day to step back, review what happened, and recalibrate. Days like September 2nd sting, but they're also the best teachers. We'll dig into why those heavy favorites stumbled, adjust our models where needed, and come back ready for the next slate.

Because here's the thing about baseball—there's always another game, another chance to get it right. That's what September is all about.
